title: Section formula
intro: In coordinate geometry, the  Section formula is a formula used to find the ratio in which a line segment is divided by a point internally or externally. It is used to find out the centroid, incenter and excenters of a triangle.

title: Segre's theorem
intro:
In projective geometry, Segre's theorem, named after the Italian mathematician Beniamino Segre, is the statement:

Any oval in a finite pappian projective plane of odd order is a nondegenerate projective conic section.
This statement was assumed 1949 by the two Finnish mathematicians G. Järnefelt and P. Kustaanheimo and its proof was published in 1955 by B. Segre.

title: Selberg's zeta function conjecture
intro: In mathematics, the Selberg conjecture, named after Atle Selberg, is a theorem about the density of zeros of the Riemann zeta function ζ(1/2 + it). It is known that the function has infinitely many zeroes on this line in the complex plane: the point at issue is how densely they are clustered.

title: Selberg trace formula
intro:
In mathematics, the Selberg trace formula, introduced by  Selberg (1956), is an expression for the character of the unitary representation of a Lie group G on the space L2(Γ\G) of square-integrable functions, where Γ is a cofinite discrete group. The character is given by the trace of certain functions on G.
The simplest case is when Γ is cocompact, when the representation breaks up into discrete summands.

title: Selman's theorem
intro: In computability theory, Selman's theorem is a theorem relating enumeration reducibility with enumerability relative to oracles. It is named after Alan Selman, who proved it as part of his PhD thesis in 1971.

title: Semi-orthogonal matrix
intro: In linear algebra, a semi-orthogonal matrix is a non-square matrix with real entries where: if the number of columns exceeds the number of rows, then the rows are orthonormal vectors; but if the number of rows exceeds the number of columns, then the columns are orthonormal vectors.

title: Separation logic
intro:
In computer science, separation logic is an extension of Hoare logic, a way of reasoning about programs.
It was developed by John C. Reynolds, Peter O'Hearn, Samin Ishtiaq and Hongseok Yang, drawing upon early work by Rod Burstall.

title: Separation principle
intro: In control theory, a separation principle, more formally known as a principle of separation of estimation and control, states that under some assumptions the problem of designing an optimal feedback controller for a stochastic system can be solved by designing an optimal observer for the state of the system, which feeds into an optimal deterministic controller for the system.  Thus the problem can be broken into two separate parts, which facilitates the design.
